string.text: The book on {TRAIT} left your party. Nothing was learned.
Choose the item to hand over. It will be kept as compensation for your lessons.
You carry the finished piece on you? Let me see it then.
Empty handed? I gave you {TRAIT} freely and asked one simple thing in return. Come back when you have completed the work.
You never brought {MASTER} the {TRAIT} piece you owed. They have forgotten about you.
{MASTER} is dead. Whatever you owed them died with them.
{MASTER} taught you {TRAIT} and expects an item bearing it in return. Make one and bring it to them.
This is fine craftsmanship. You have done well and you are ready to learn more enchantments.
The challenge stands. You have {DAYS} day(s) to face {MASTER}'s apprentice.

The ground comes up to meet you. You wake some time later, bruised to the bone and short of the breath to argue.{newline}{newline}{MASTER}'s verdict is brief: train your magic, and come back when you are worth teaching.

{MASTER} leads you out to an arena they prepared. Their apprentice, {APPRENTICE}, is already waiting and is armed, armoured, and entirely unbothered by the sight of you.{newline}{newline}You fight until one of you cannot stand. Nobody is here to die. Your magic is your own to use.
{APPRENTICE} goes down hard, beaten but breathing.{newline}{newline}Return to {MASTER} and inform them of your deed.
You let the week {MASTER} gave you run out without facing their apprentice. They have made their judgement of you.
{MASTER} is dead. Whatever they meant to teach you died with them.
{MASTER} will not teach you {SPELL} until you have beaten their apprentice in single combat.
You have beaten {MASTER}'s apprentice. Return to them to claim {SPELL}.
{MASTER}'s apprentice left you in the dust. They will not hear you again for some time.
The arcane traditions of the world and those known to practice them.
No practitioners of this tradition are known to you.
This art is wielded by no clans. Its few masters are hidden, and none are known to you yet.
You have not identified this practitioner. Find them in the world or ask after them in a tavern.
Interested in the craft? Very well, I am willing to part with a formula, but I'll want a piece made with it in return.
Your enchantments. I would learn the craft.
You hold every formula I would part with, {STUDENT}. There is nothing new for you here.
The item is unmade. You keep part of its reagents.
You carry nothing that holds an enchantment.
Choose the enchanted items to unmake. Half of each reagent cost comes back to you, a third if you crafted the item yourself.
Between a scribe's shop and a shuttered apothecary you find {SETTLEMENT_NAME}'s enchanter's quarter. Reagent jars line the shelves, and the air smells faintly of scorched copper.
Knows {COUNT} enchantment(s) but lacks the skill or lore for any of them.
Choose who in your party will use their skills to enchant equipment.
No one in your party knows any enchantment yet. Books and masters can teach you.
The enchanter has nothing to sell.
An item can carry at most {MAX_TRAITS} enchantment(s).
You lack the reagents for this work.
No one in your party knows an enchantment that fits this item.
{HERO} knows no enchantment that fits this item.
The work holds. The item is in your inventory.
The local nightwatch is onto you. Face the consequences of your vile actions.
The graveyard's massive iron gates are closed shut.
You have arrived at {SETTLEMENT_NAME}'s graveyard. Graves, tombstones and family crypts litter the peaceful hillside.
Raise dead from the corpses in the ground (wait 8 hours).
The common folk's graves are ripe for the taking. You spend the night hours dragging corpses from the ground and binding them to your will.
You drag {COUNT} more from the earth to serve you.
Speak. You will have your freedom.
Your freedom is worth more to me than your gossip. Get comfortable.
I know something, but I will not hand it to you through these bars for the pleasure of your company. Open the door, give me a horse, and my knowledge is yours.
Yes, {MASTER} is said to walk a forbidden path that most tremble at. What you do with this information is of your own accord.
Forbidden magic? Bah, I know nothing of such superstitions, and neither does anyone worth listening to.
Whispers only. They say {CLAN} keeps a secret they would kill to protect. Ask among that clan, if you have the stomach for it.
You think me afraid? I hide nothing, I simply don't advertise. What you say is true, now what is it you want of me?
I have spoken with those who keep your clan's secrets. I know what you are. Shall we speak plainly, or shall I say it louder?
They say someone in these lands practices forbidden magic. What do you know of it?
A lead: {CLAN} hides a practitioner of forbidden magic. Capture one of its own to learn who.
The truth is out: {NAME} is a hidden master of the {TRADITION}.
A name at last: {NAME} is said to be the one practicing forbidden magic. Time to confront them.
You have my ear, {STUDENT}. What is it you seek?
Your magic. I would learn a spell.

That's all of it, and also none of it. Every mixture, every ratio, everything I know is yours. Now go out there and find something that can put a hole through the horizon. I have some theories... but nothing concrete.

I do believe you now know virtually everything I do. Forgive me, this occasion usually calls for ceremony but it's been so long that I honestly do not remember the words. You are now a Loremaster. But the work continues. The work always continues.

That's the last of it. Everything my master taught me and what I managed to work out on my own. ...This never happened before, so I'm not quite sure what to say. Safe travels? Just don't go dying recklessly now.

Tha's all the tales I carry, lad, n' all the words I know.{newline}Not one of em was ever mine, they came from long ago.{newline}Go tell em proper someplace else, n' tell em nice n' slow,{newline}for one day thou'lt be in one, lad, n' someone else shall know.
That is all of Aqshy I have to give. When they whisper your name in that frightened manner they often use, do let them know who your master was. It is after all professional courtesy.
You see it all now don't you? I have granted you eyes. Behold the sky in all its glory! Oh how the patterns swirl and churn unending. Every eventuality...
That's everything I have. Use it wisely and don't forget to pass it on, preferably while you're still above the ground.
That is the last of it. You no longer require my instruction, Hierophant. Now you hold the line. Dismissed!

You have them all now, my apprentice, all my notes. Every trial, every failure, the whole damn ledger. Now go out there and find something I got wrong. I shall be furious! And delighted... to finally have a peer!

Everything! You have everything! Oh how quickly you've grown, my little morsel. And now that I've taught you all I know, I find I have no further use for you. Ha! Be at rest, 'twas just a jest, your heart shall remain inside your chest.
You have mastered the whole of Minor Magic, should we call you a Minor Master now I wonder?
The master will teach you for a price.
{COUNT} of your men march with {PARTY} now, their minds no longer their own.
Rebuilt the world: removed magic from {REMOVED} hero(es) and generated a new set of wizards.

Rival Wizards settings restored to their defaults. The boxes on screen may still show the old numbers, but the defaults are what will be saved. Press Done to apply them and rebuild your world. Pressing Cancel discards this.
Could not restore the defaults. See the SOTOR log for details.
No campaign is loaded. Start or load a game first.
{EXTRA} of them inherited the gift from their parents.
Wizard lords: {LORDS} Hidden masters: {HIDDEN} Tavern casters: {TAVERN}
Rival Wizards is switched OFF, so this world would have no wizards at all.
This is an estimate. Changes will not be applied until you press Done and restart.
Could not read the campaign. See the SOTOR log for details.
The arena masters permit no conjured servants.
SOTOR: sotor_overrides.xml could not be read, so ALL of your overrides were ignored. Usually a missing '/>' or quote. ({ERROR})
Gain access to adept level spells. Unlocks the ability to learn the Lore of Necromancy.
Any buffs you cast on a friendly unit will now also apply to you even if you are not in range.
As formation Captain, all troops in your formation deal additional 10% magic damage.
Become an Archmage. Unlocks the restricted High Magic and Dark Magic lores, and lets you set two enchantments on a single item.
For every enchanted item in your equipment slots you gain +5 extra Winds of magic at the start of battle.
You gain +20% Winds of Magic regeneration while waiting in a town.
Damage dealt by your damaging spells is reduced by 15%, but troops in your formation take 30% less damage from spells.
Your instant damaging and healing spells are 20% less effective, but cost 30% less winds of magic.
Your Winds of Magic is set to 25 if you have less than that at the beginning of the battle.
You gain 25% more Spellcraft experience from casting spells.
Learning new spells and lores costs 50% less gold.
Gain access to master level spells.
Gain access to entry level spells.
Your instant damaging and healing spells are 20% more effective but cost 30% more winds of magic.
Your damaging spells do 90% reduced damage to yourself.
Your self targeted buff spells have 50% more duration.
Every companion in your party gains 1000 experience in a random skill per day.
Your party gains a permanent +5 increase to party morale.
Your damaging spells do 30% less damage to troops in your party.
You never finished drilling {SPELL}, and {MASTER} has lost track of you.
{MASTER} is dead. There is no one left to judge your practice.
Return to {MASTER} and show him what you have learned.
No? Then stop wasting my time and make up your mind.
You would rummage through my mind like a purse for coins? Fine, which one?
Take one formula and your prisoner will go free.
I hold no formula that you do not already know.
Then choose, and choose quickly. Which of them?
Teach me your magics, and I may yet let you walk free.
You are a fool. But a merciful one.
Very well. Listen carefully. I will say this only once before I take my leave of you.
You have everything I know already, and I have nothing left to buy my freedom with. Kill me or keep me, but stop wasting my time.
Keep your secrets and go, I release you.
You would wring the secrets of {LORE_NAME} from me for my freedom? Say what it is you want, and be plain about it.
Your lore. Open it to me, and you walk out of here.
Your enchanting secrets. One formula, and you go free.
One spell. Teach it, and you go free.
Very well. Attend me closely. The formula of {TRAIT}, every measure and every word. Commit it to paper, and I shall take my leave.
Cutting through bureaucracy with sheer force, are we? Then you are already a Doomweaver in spirit. Good. You'll need that if you hope to master Dhar.

Well this is a rare thing indeed. I can sense you truly have the knack for it. It would be a shame for such talent to go to waste now, wouldn't it? I give you Qhaysh, my captor. Please do not disappoint me.
So this is how it goes. Fine, Ghur's yours. It never belonged to me anyway and at least now there's another Shaman out there. Now get these off me.

Thou'st put these ancient hands in irons ta make me speak my part.{newline}Shyish was never mine ta keep, so take it, take the art.{newline}But there's a jest in what thou'st done, n' here it is for free:{newline}death would have found thee soon enough. Thou needn't have troubled me.
Unhand me and it is yours. Aqshy will answer to you now, freely given. Do note that word when you tell the story, for I would far rather be remembered for my generosity.
Oh, don't look so pleased with yourself. I saw this. Not clearly, but I saw it, and I came anyway. Here, Azyr is yours as it was always meant to be.
Chains, how quaint. Fine, here's Ghyran, take it. Nothing in nature is ever truly yours, it is simply your turn. Though I would have preferred a conversation.

You want Hysh? Then take it and be quick about it. I have been on the losing side of a rout and I know what becomes of prisoners who bore their captors. It is yours. I warn you, you'll find it much less pliable than me.

Restraints? Truly? Shall I turn them to gold? Or perhaps rust them away? I simply cannot decide. Very well, Chamon is yours, the basic principles that is. Let's see what you can manage on your own. I am keeping my notes.
Chains! Oh marvelous, my little morsel, you are a natural! Yes, yes, take it, the Ninth Book lies open for you, oh I could weep with pride. Do loosen these though. My wrists are coming apart.
You went to all this trouble... for Minor Magic? Take it. Take it and never tell a soul for your own sake.
Lacks the lore or the caster level this text demands.
Oh, you. You have quite some nerve, don't you? Or are you just thick? Fine, I'll teach you, but only if you give me another battle like the last one. Show me it wasn't luck!
You may have the raw talent but wisdom takes time. Come back to me when you have outgrown your need for misadventure, and we shall explore the secrets of magic together.

I've been called a savage my whole life by men like you with your soft palms and clean boots. You took a shortcut which defeats the whole point of Ghur. You want the rest? Learn it yourself like I did.
A tale that's forced ain't worth the tellin', lad.{newline}Nor is it worth the hearin' twice.{newline}It comes out thin n' bare n' sad.{newline}So do not ask me thrice.
You had me in chains. Chains! And now you want lessons? I will teach you nothing. Whatever you manage from here on out you shall manage alone, and you will leave my name out of it.

I have taught you this already, a hundred times, in a hundred futures of a hundred lifetimes. It went the way you would expect. Forgive me if I decline. I did not become an Astromancer to spend a season on something so dreadfully dull.
No, and not out of spite. You can't grow an oak in barren soil, and I've had a glimpse of what's between your ears. A fine young sprout you are not.
Instruction is a privilege, not war spoils. I shall not teach an enemy, former or otherwise. You want it? Come and take it.

Ha! Couldn't manage it, could you? A colleague I would teach. A patron I would tolerate. A captor and also a helpless amateur? No, you shall not have my method, and you will no doubt get every part of it wrong. That is punishment enough.

Oh, but you have all that you need from me, morsel, and now you demand the rest for free? No, no, no. I shall not spoil our burgeoning little prodigy with my instruction. That is how I learned, you see. Go out there and take it!
You put me in irons over children's charms. No. Go find a hedge witch to teach you your parlor tricks.
You saw forbidden winds in that battle. {NAME} is one of the {TRADITION}.
{NAME}, of the {TRADITION}. Their people hold {WHERE}, off to the {DIRECTION}. You didn't hear it from me.
I am looking for someone who commands the arcane arts.
Sorcerers? Not round here. Try the bigger towns, or ask further afield.
Your mastery of the Winds of Magic. Higher Spellcraft increases spell damage and unlocks higher spell tiers.
Seek out a master or companion to teach you
No one in your clan knows this lore
+{AMOUNT} standing with the {TRADITION} for fighting alongside {NAME}.
You gained standing with {TRADITIONS}, and the {LORD_COUNT} lords who follow those traditions.
You lost standing with {TRADITIONS}, and the {LORD_COUNT} lords who follow those traditions.
Your standing with the {TRADITION} fell by {AMOUNT}, and by {LORD_AMOUNT} with the {LORD_COUNT} lords who follow them.
Your standing with the {TRADITION} fell by {AMOUNT}.
Your standing with the {TRADITION} rose by {AMOUNT}, and by {LORD_AMOUNT} with the {LORD_COUNT} lords who follow them.
Your standing with the {TRADITION} rose by {AMOUNT}.
You cannot raise the dead over open water.
You already carry {LORE}, so I do not need to repeat the basics. You are now my student. Ask me for a spell and we shall see your worth.
I have no answer to that.
I would honor your teachings and spread the word of your good name.
Your name deserves better recognition amongst our peers. Teach me, and I will see that it is spoken properly.
The world needs more of us who can wield these magics wisely, and fewer who cannot.
I hold all eight, which makes me answerable to all eight. A gap in one is a duty I am failing.
I have closed wounds and watched men die of things nobody could name. I know what the winds do to a body.
I can knit a wound shut and still not say what the winds do inside a man. Teach me that to which you have dedicated your life.
A man in your position collects secrets, and secrets find the wrong ear. I would rather owe you a kindness.
I know of some of your... colorful activities, and have told no one. I would rather that stayed a courtesy between us.
I have faced worse than your magics and lived. Teach me, if you are so great.
I hold all eight, true, but you have lived inside one your whole life. That is the sort of expertise I came for.
My clan has land, coin, and a long memory for those who help it. You would find us generous.
Ask anything of my clan and it is done. I would sooner be in your debt than go on not knowing this.
I know what this magic is worth on a field of battle. In the wrong hands it is a waste, but not in mine.
All wizards have a theory until they get a fireball to the face. Show me actual application.
Name your price. Coin, a favour owed, a share of the spoils. I pay my debts.
I will not haggle with you as though this were grain. But should you be curious about a spell of mine I would perhaps accommodate.
I wish to learn the arcane arts you command.
Bring him out. I will face him.
Then go and prepare. You have {DAYS} day(s). Come to me after that and you will find I have nothing to say to you.
Before I teach you any further you must prove yourself, {STUDENT}. Defeat my current apprentice in a wizard duel, and {SPELL} is yours.
Have you found your nerve, {STUDENT}? My apprentice is waiting, and you have {DAYS} day(s) left of the week I gave you.
You knocked my apprentice on his arse. Very well, a bargain is a bargain. Listen closely...
Hm? Who are you again? Ah. My apprentice. I had wondered where you had got to. What did you need?
You messed with the weave and broke something, Wizlet. Speak to me again and we will begin afresh.
So you wish to learn my magics, then? Give me a good reason.
My magics are too strong for you {STUDENT}. Find yourself a master who can teach you weaker magic.
{MASTER} has opened {LORE} to you. Return to learn its spells.
So you would learn {LORE}. Convince me you are worth the risk.
You? Asking me? You hold all eight winds at once, and you want {LORE} from my hands. ...Are you testing me? Convince me you're serious.
So, you wish to further your knowledge of {LORE} and learn {SPELL}? Convince me.
A Loremaster at my door asking after {SPELL}. You could likely reason it out yourself without much effort. So why come to me?
So. You have been busy with {SPELL}. Good, you have earned the right to ask me for more.
Not yet, {STUDENT}. I gave you {SPELL} and you have barely used it. Go and put it to work, then come back to me.
You reek of {LORE}! Get out of my sight, {PRACTITIONER}!
Feeble Wizlet! Do you really think you can manage the glories that are my spells?
You already know every spell I could teach you. Find yourself a greater master than I.

I am flattered you even thought to ask, Loremaster. But you already hold everything I could offer, and a great deal more. Should I ever stumble onto something new, you will be the first to hear of it.
You again? We discussed this already and my answer has not changed. Do not bother me for another {SOTOR_RETRY_DAYS} days.
Who has brought this filthy peasant before me? Guards! Throw him out!
Our people are at war. They'd have me drawn and quartered if I taught an enemy.
Which of them, then? Name it.

Shamans keep to the wild places and take the strength and the shape of beasts for their own. They hold few halls and fewer titles, and the courts of the great clans regard them as little better than the animals they command.

Doomweavers take the winds raw and unsorted, and pay for that power in a coin they do not name. No clan flies their colours. They are one or two hidden souls inside a great hall, and finding one is a labour of its own.

Spirit Magisters walk the purple wind at the border of dying, taking the will out of an enemy before ever taking his life. They insist they are nothing like the necromancers, and the necromancers agree.

Pyromancers draw on the red wind and answer with fire, favouring the swift and total ruin of whatever stands before them. Even allied captains keep their powder and their tents well clear of a Pyromancer's tent.

Astromancers read the turning of the heavens and call down its lightning and its storms. They are trusted as counsellors and feared as omens, for they are said to know a battle's end before it is joined.

Loremasters hold all the winds at once in a discipline that most who attempt it do not survive. No clan flies their colours. They are one or two hidden souls inside a great hall, and finding one is a labour of its own.
Druids draw on the green wind that runs through root and blood, closing wounds and calling the living land to fight beside them. They are welcome in villages that would turn any other wizard away.
Hierophants wield the white wind as a lantern and a blade, burning what should not walk and mending what should. They are the traditional enemies of the necromancer and the Doomweaver alike.

Alchemists work the yellow wind through ore and edge, hardening their own arms and rotting the arms of their enemies. They are the most respected of wizards among smiths, quartermasters and paymasters.
Necromancers refuse the border of dying altogether and raise what lies beneath the field to march again. Where a Necromancer holds a clan, that clan does not want for soldiers.

Dark Magic or 'Dhar' as it's named. I'm sure you've heard it called something worse. The other orders each take one wind and spend a lifetime learning to hold it politely, but really who exactly are they trying to impress? There are eight winds and so we use all eight of them together. They don't always mesh well so sometimes you just need to force it. This can have some disastrous results, but that's exactly where the power comes from. They call us Doomweavers. Such a fancy name for such a simple concept. We don't have a philosophy and hold nothing in reverence. Magic is a tool, plain and simple. Everything I teach you will break something or someone, maybe even yourself if you're not careful. So ask questions and listen carefully because it's going to be a lot of work.

Before you learn a single spell, understand what you have been looking at. Magic was once whole and an undivided silvery haze over everything. Then it was broken by people who had good reasons but insufficient foresight, and the eight winds are what fell out of the wreck. Every order you have met studies a shard and calls it a discipline. Qhaysh means holding all eight in harmony rather than choosing one and calling the choice a philosophy. Yes, I know all eight of the other lores adequately, which is the minimum requirement to begin here. This prerequisite is why our order is so small. You will no doubt hear whispers that we do what the Doomweavers do. And while this is technically correct, it misses all the nuance. We do not force the eight winds together in a destructive collision. Instead we... persuade them, which takes considerably longer and does not disfigure the practitioner.

You won't find a college for our lore. No tower, no dome, not even a library. Does that bother you? Bothers some more than it should. They call us Shamans when they're being polite, and file the Lore of Beasts under "primal thaumaturgy," a great many syllables for a thing they've never once tried to understand. Ghur is heard and not seen, and it's loudest where there's no one else to hear it. So what would we do with a building? I've had students leave over this. Do as you like.

There was a village once what would not bury up their dead.{newline}Cheaper ta keep em at their labor, or so it was said.{newline}'Leven years the harvest came in fat n' fair n' ahead.{newline}Then the corpses took a count, found themselves the greater number,{newline}rose up ta settle the score n' tore the livin' all asunder.{newline}I know, for I were there ta see the last of em go under.{newline}I tell thee this for one day thou shalt stand accused the same,{newline}by some loud mouth'd blaggard what can't tell releasin' from a claim.{newline}We're the Spirit Magisters, whate'er the street sees fit ta name.{newline}Shyish blows from all what's ended, through all what hath not.{newline}Hear an endin' proper, lad, n' fear neither grave nor rot.

Pyromancy is the art of invoking and manipulating fire. Aqshy, rather. And the far harder art of keeping it under control. Any fool with some flint can start a fire. I am teaching you to do it without immolating yourself as well. You will learn, for instance, that plate armor is merely a cooking vessel, and that the men wearing it have never once worked this out. Enjoy their screams, but never grow careless around it. I have seen many a Wizlet turn themselves to ash. Amusing, certainly. But don't you dare lose control, as your failures would stain my reputation.

Astromancy is the art of reading and manipulating the heavens. Storms, comets, the hour of a man's death... all of it is written, and all of it can be controlled. Ah, Azyr, most distant of the winds. It gathers far above our heads and recognizes no boundary of time. Learn to channel it and you will glimpse the sea of eventualities... only glimpse. No eyes were built wide enough for more. A man who knows the shape of tomorrow is never truly at war, he always arrives at the right place and at the right time.

We Druids are the practitioners of the Lore of Life, but there's nothing truly special about our magic. I'm sure you've heard legends of us healing the sick and wounded, stopping plagues, curing famine. Nonsense, we simply manipulate the natural cycle of life. For growth and rot are the same process viewed from opposite ends, and Ghyran attends to both without preference. Your friends, your enemies, your own body, all of it will grow and all of it will die. Nature cares not, and I have made my peace with that.

Stand there. Feet apart, hands down, eyes forward. They call it the Lore of Light, but light is the least of it. I will drill that lesson into you. Hysh was the first of the winds, and everything made since must defer to its presence. Our light cannot be resisted. It cannot be refused. You are now a Hierophant. You do not grasp, you hold. You do not move. Master stillness and very little in creation will be permitted to argue. Stop! You are already fidgeting.

So you want to be an Alchemist? My apprentice? I should warn you that I ramble sometimes and you may interrupt me. Quiet! The Lore of Metal, they call it. Alchemy. What we do here is not really magic, it is closer to natural philosophy except that I am permitted to cheat! Chamon is the heavy wind and it sticks to metal the way ink takes to paper. Which is to say reliably! Well, 80% of the time. Do you know how rare that is among wizards? I can run the same experiment eleven times and get the same result eleven times, no matter how much the subjects squirm. The others find this dull. Dull! Their muddled heads are full of abstract prophecies and here I am documenting empirical truth.

Ah yes! Do come sit down anywhere you like. Mind the smell, it's mine. They tell you necromancy is all about the dead. Hogwash! The exact bloody opposite! It is about control of all life and surpassing the tyranny of death! And believe me I have, for a long, long time. Ha! Look at my hands, morsel. Go on, look. That is what the Ninth Book costs, and I would gladly pay it all again tomorrow. Necromancy is not a practice of that watery Shyish the Magisters sip at. Our Dhar takes and takes but then it gives you everything, including time! And time is the only thing worth having, and you, my little morsel, are running out of it the longer we waste on pleasantries. Tick tock. So let's get started!
I don't know how you convinced me to teach you Minor Magic but this 'lore' is so simple we usually teach it to children. Surely you cannot screw this up?

The amaranth doth keep her color long past cut n' dried.{newline}A flower what will not admit the day that she hath died.{newline}Wear that stubbornness thyself n' poison passeth by,{newline}n' plague n' rot n' fouled water leave thee well n' dry.{newline}But mark me twice, for here's the whole n' honest of the writ:{newline}I said thou shalt not sicken. Never said thou shalt not wilt.

A spear. Yes, an actual spear. I've watched grown wizards wrinkle their noses at this one. Pour Ghur into the shaft until it hums and then throw it like you mean it. Goes through armor, goes through the man, keeps going. Two thousand generations of hunters can't all have been wrong.

Recall what I told you about the silver haze. This is the closest anyone has come to putting it back. Weave all eight winds into a temporary equilibrium and pour that energy into a wounded man, and he will be... corrected. Restored to the condition his body was meant to be in. Stronger and faster than he has ever been, or ever will be again. But it is a fleeting sensation, for, alas, perfection cannot be maintained in nature. I find that most weep after the experience and they can never really explain why.

Thou needst not aim this cleverly nor seek a gap in mail.{newline}Steel means nothin' ta what comes, nor shield, nor coat o' scale.{newline}Call it down upon the ground n' all what stood there turns ta gray.{newline}No wound, no blood, no body. Just the ash n' what blows away.
A simple protection spell that may prove useful. This is the elementary form of more sophisticated magics.

Put your hand on that trunk and push. Harder. It resists because it has nothing to prove and nowhere to be. That is what you will lay over your soldiers. Their skin will thicken and dull, and blades chip upon their flesh. But it will fade and the damage will come back eventually in some other form.

Now the harder lesson. Light came before the hour, so the hour must yield. Draw the light in close about your body and feel the space around you distort. The body stands still but the space bends around you and you cross the battlefield in a flash of light. Stillness is speed. Speed is power. Do not question it.

Beyond our world exist countless others with horrors that can melt a man's mind, but anything can be weaponized. Tear the seam between realities and something comes through that has no business being here, and its fury can usually be pointed at your enemies. It stays for just as long as the tear remains open, but that's not always the case, as the late Arnzipal would no doubt attest.

High enough above us, the air is cruel. It hates the living and freezes without mercy. Take it. Pull that place down and onto your enemies, let them congeal blades in hand, solidify, stiffen, perfectly preserved as all things should be.

A simple bolt of fire. Point your hand and melt your enemy. There is no technique to it and no artistry in it, and you will use it more than everything else I teach you combined. I suppose we all have to start somewhere...

A bit of Shyish in the mix for this one. Yes, Shyish, don't make that face, the Spirit Magisters do not own it. Bind it to the flames and you get a skull, burning, that tears through enemy formations like a vengeful god. I have seen it incinerate thousands and I still do not tire of the sight. Try it.

Not one rightly knows what Laniph were. A queen. A witch.{newline}A madwoman gone thin n' strange n' buried in a ditch.{newline}What's known is that she killed n' killed n' left no mark on skin.{newline}The purple light comes up close as a breath, n' then it draws thee in.{newline}It squeezes till the heart gives way n' he drops where he stood.{newline}But choose thy targets carefully, the stout ones are no good.

A Pyromancer's greatest enemy is always themselves. Fire does not distinguish between the man casting it and the man receiving, so we cheat by wearing it. Wreathe yourself in flame and the heat disperses laterally, avoiding your ripe pink flesh. Mind you, it lasts only as long as your concentration. Requires a bit of attention span, this one. But hopefully yours is long enough to spare you the most embarrassing death our order offers.

You have heard the tales I imagine. A sphere of light that drifts through a shuttered window, circles a room, chooses one man out of ten and leaves the rest untouched? Sailors call it "corpse candle", priests name it "judgment", and scholars insist it is nothing at all. Fools the lot of them! It is Azyr, bright holy Azyr! Pooled and wandering, looking for somewhere to go.

There's no lore for cold. No color, no institution. Yet somewhere far north they've made an entire discipline of it and nobody here has bothered to learn how. Doesn't matter, here's my take on it. Force enough Dhar together in a particular way and you get the same result without needing to understand anything about it. Not the strongest spell in our repertoire but certainly the cheapest and the easiest to cast. It also numbs whoever survives it. Frozen hands can't draw a bow.

If ever you tire of burning things, and I cannot imagine why you would, there is this. Solidified magma thrown in fragments like primates throwing poo. It works, in the sense that a rock works. There are better uses of your time and mine, but you asked, and here we are.

Beyond the heavens your naked eye can bear lie countless bodies, some smaller than our own and some vast beyond reckoning. An endless armory just above our heads... and no one thinks to reach for it! You need only give one a push. Let the world below do the rest.

Aenarion is a name from long before the breaking, and the sources contradict each other on everything except for his bravery and the speed at which he fought. Weave the eight and speak his name, and every ally near you will forget their fear and find their blows landing quicker than their arms should permit. I do not know what special power the name holds but the spell fizzles without it. Perhaps this is the very first instance of magical copyright. Do bear in mind that Aenarion is said to have lived his entire life in this condition, and it did not end well for him or for anyone standing nearby.

Saw a mercenary company break to this once. Two hundred men, good armor, no casualties to speak of. They just got tired of it. Sprites in the eyes and the mouth and under the mail, biting, and nothing to swing at. They walked off the field. Whole thing took a quarter hour and nobody could say what killed them, because nothing did.

A hex is rarely anything more than a charm run backwards. I wish more people understood this, because half the curses in the world are some old protective working that an untrained wizard botched. Take a ward against arrows, reverse the flow, and it will attract projectiles instead. Cast it on an enemy formation and your peasant levies will shoot like veterans of thirty years. They will credit themselves, of course. Let them bask in their ignorance.

There was a tongue spoken when the world was young, and it is gone. Three words survive. Three! I do not know what they mean and I will not pretend to... but say them into a company of men and trigger the inverse of spherical harmony. Learn them exactly. Kha'ronis. Vel'thuun. Azyrath!

Time is the thief that has been at us since the day we were born, but there are ways to redirect and intensify its flow. Spit the words out and watch it take them. Their hair will go white, their skin will draw in tight over the bone, and it will quicken and worsen and they will plead with every breath they have left. Armor won't save them, nothing will. Oh how they beg. Their voice gradually turning older and older until they cannot form the words any longer. It is such a delight on the ears.
I once taught this spell to a child that had not yet learned to speak. He took to casting it at his parents when he was hungry.

Azyr and Aqshy in equal quantities, force them together into the same shape and hold them there until they're about to explode, then release. The bolt is the Azyr, the burst is the Aqshy decompressing at unnatural speeds. Anything left standing is set alight. If the Astromancers and Pyromancers ever set aside their differences and worked together, they could destroy all of creation, but you'd have better luck reconciling oil and water.

Light can be hard or soft. Hold it too tightly and it turns brittle like glass. Then you break it. The shards will find the first men standing in front of you and bury themselves in whatever they touch. Aim once. They will not travel past the first rank, so choose wisely.

The high and mighty Astromancers pull rocks out of the sky and take enormous pride in it. Same principle here, but you pack the thing with Dhar before it lands. The sky opens, and what comes down is black and burning and arrives with more explosive force than any comet could possibly have. It punches through armor, ships, castle walls, even dragons if you ever meet one. Careful not to get caught in the impact crater.

Everything alive is either taking or being taken from. No matter what your priests tell you, there are no bystanders in the great game. Open a channel between yourself and your enemies and their strength will run downhill towards you. They will wither and turn into fertilizer for your growth. Their life pays for yours. But you have changed nothing for all remains equal.
An amusing method to unhorse those uppity knights. More fun than effective, truly.

Beneath the earth lies an entire world of hidden life, matching the variety found on the surface. Though few people ever see these secret creatures, this spell lets you call them forth to honor your enemies by returning them to the earth's natural cycle.
Why would you wish to fight like a peasant if you already know magic? Oh fine...

Bjuna were a warrior grand what never cracked a grin.{newline}Sixty year o' stone-faced glory, not one chuckle got within.{newline}Then a fool let slip a jest n' found the crack n' got it in.{newline}Laughed until his sides gave way, he laughed until they split.{newline}Now whose fate were worse, thou reckons? His, or his servin' boys what's left ta scrape the pit?

While everything else I have taught you has been about balance, this spell has some... stylistic disharmony. You weave the eight, then deliberately let Aqshy slip its restraint and utter the one secret word I shall teach you. Ashaellu. Do not write it down. But do commit it to memory, for once you speak it the fire shall take the shape of a great bird and swoop down on your enemies. Those not consumed outright shall burn until they perish, and the only witnesses take the word to their graves.

To transmute one metal you must sacrifice another. The first alchemical law, no doubt written by the insufficiently curious. Flesh, as it turns out, was never accounted for. Force enough Chamon through a man and he does not merely die, he changes into something solid, gleaming, permanent, and considerably more valuable than he was a moment ago. I ask you, of all the deaths in this world, is there truly any more glorious than this?

Ah yes, the spell no one shuts up about. Tell me, did you decide to become a Pyromancer just to learn this one? Bah, tis no matter. Gather Aqshy until your palms blister, then throw it and let it come apart where it lands. Everything within twenty paces catches at once, including the ground and the air. Elegant? Well yes, actually. There is elegance in simplicity and nothing else clears out vermin in such an efficient way.

Any Wizlet can hurl a ball of fire at an enemy. Only a master can hold that fire open into a vortex that devours all within. Cast it into a packed formation and you will learn the name of every god in creation, one scream at a time.

A blade is a peasant's weapon, but even such crude utensils can be improved. Channel Aqshy down through the hilt until the steel glows white and burns more than it cuts. Armor, shield, bone, it makes no distinction and leaves all wounds nice and cauterized. No risk of blood on your cloak. Do try not to enjoy yourself too much with this one, it's unseemly.

Crows have been following armies and feeding on corpses since long before anybody could write it down. They know what a battle is and what it means. Call enough of them and they won't wait for the fighting to finish, they'll go straight for the eyes, hundreds of little wounds and no way to guard against any of them. It's not dignified but it works.
Disgusting! You want me to teach you what? Fine then...

Three syllables. That is all Gehenna left us, no notes whatsoever, or none that survived the fire. Next time use retardant paper, amateur. Nevertheless, say the words and hurl the sphere, and it will roll through a formation leaving nothing but slag and the smell. Not transmutation, mind you, nothing so refined. Simply metal at temperatures it was never meant to reach. Crude but effective. I have a garden of failed attempts and I water them regularly.

Gehenna's again, and this time he did leave notes, and frankly the penmanship is appalling. Molten gold, held in the shape of a hound? Not machines at least, nothing so crude as gears. But they work. Blow the whistle and they shall rampage across the battlefield. They do not tire, they do not lose the scent, and they do not stop when the screaming starts. I have improved the hips.

Yes, out of the forehead. I know, I have tried every other point of exit and the forehead is the only one that doesn't disfigure the caster, so stop grumbling. It leaves you, it vanishes, and then it pierces a man and melts him from the inside. Never misses, either! Not once in four hundred trials. It does have to get through his armor like anything else, so aim for the head! So many generals are too proud to wear helmets. You would think they'd learn. They never do!

Far, far below the earth lie the corpses of battles so ancient that every record of them is lost. Dig with a shovel and you get last winter's paupers. Reach deeper, morsel, and you shall pull out the champions of old. You could even call us the premiere archaeologists of this world! Who else brings the past back in such a visceral form? Truly we honor the poor sods of this world with a chance to meet their ancestors in a river of blood!

It's not actually hail, it's a bunch of falling rocks. Lift a few hundred of them out of the riverbed and put them in the air then stop holding them. Armor doesn't help. Shields don't help. This is how men killed each other before anyone thought of any magic, and if it ain't broke don't fix it.

When the spheres are in harmony, the world beneath them falls into place. Men do not stumble. Blades do not find the gaps in their armor. Reach into the sea of eventualities and pluck every future in which they fail. What remains must, by definition, be victory. Your men will never know why they could not be killed... let them thank their gods.

Your men will want to die. They will lie there and bleed and consider it. But you will not permit this. Pour the light into their wounds and let them bathe in it. Hysh is far older than their pathetic mortality. Do not ask them if they can stand. Forbid them to die. You will not always manage it. Do it anyway.

The simplest gift of the storm, but the most memorable. Reach up, little Wizlet, take hold of what is already gathering above you, and let it fall! Any peasant who has watched a tree split in a storm understands this spell already. But you... you will choose the tree!

Ordinary armor is so last century. A smith hammering a flat sheet is almost adorable, wouldn't you agree? Instead we invite Chamon into the metal until it becomes one with the man inside it, and then it will turn a blow the way a mountain turns weather. Do not ask me what meteors have to do with it. That came from my publicist, I would have named it "dense phase viscosity experiment v5".

Some consider this forbidden, and I understand the objection, but "forbidden" is a committee word. Not one a deep thinker would keep in their repertoire. A mind is a structure like any other, and years of study will teach you its ins and outs and demystify its sacred connotations. Once you understand it, you may take hold of the mind, and the man attached to it. Command him and he will fight for you as sincerely as he fought against you a moment before. Ask yourself what is truly more merciful for an adversary: a gruesome death, or a life of useful service that he will perhaps never remember?
An elementary spell to prevent death on the battlefield. Though you might just die from embarrassment if someone witnesses you cast it.

Ah, now this is my little masterpiece. Your servants come apart for that is simply what they do, but nothing that has already died can truly die a second time. Breathe in Dhar, then exhale darkness and let it fill the gaps. Bone knits with bone, sinew finds sinew, and flesh melds with flesh. They will stand up as though nothing had happened. They won't thank you of course but you will feel great satisfaction. Careful using it on yourself or you might end up with hands like mine.

This one is his. The great one's own, straight from the Book, and the fact that I can cast it without dissolving should tell you precisely who you are dealing with. It is only looking, morsel. Fix your eyes on a living man and let the Dhar out through them, and watch him go gray and dry and empty while he is still standing up, still trying to speak. That is the moment I do this all for. Not the corpse but the face he makes just before he becomes one.

Hands up, fingers spread. A net of Hysh makes the perfect trap for tight unit formations. It is not thrown. You hold them as long as you command them to stay. The threads of light are virtually unbreakable. Halt their movements and they will be defenseless as you rain down holy fire. Do not drop your hands.

Pann was a real person no matter what you hear scholars say. He walked out of a bear fight without a mark on him and would not explain how, and I spent eleven years working it out. Guess I'm giving it to you for free. Thicken the hide until steel feels like nothing. Your men won't be pretty afterward, but they'll be alive, and that's good enough for me.

Pha never lost a man he was paying attention to and neither will you. He taught me this standing exactly where you are standing. It might seem like a wall around your men but it's really a fog around your enemies. Every arrow and every blade will go a hand's width wide off target. The enemy will believe himself unlucky. Not so, he is simply being refused.

Look at them, clad heel to toe in iron, each convinced they're safe because a man with a hammer promised them. Well, iron oxidizes! It has always loved to rust, and the smiths continue their futile postponing. So unpostpone it. Cast it once and the armor sags, then flakes, then crumbles! A proud noble sir in full regalia... reduced to standing naked and covered in orange dust! Has there ever been a sight more amusing, I ask?

The winds all come from the same place, and by the time they reach us they've been strained through the vortex and sorted into colors. Walk it a step upstream. Reach back to where it comes from and take it raw and unfiltered, as much as you can hold, then hand it to your forces and watch them work. Some will go mad with frenzy but that power will be directed towards your enemies. The effect fades quickly. Don't use it on men you intend to keep.

There was a tribe long gone afore the oldest name I know,{newline}what worshipped up a sun that give no warmth n' cast no glow.{newline}Fed the thing its proper due n' it would feed em back in kind.{newline}Missed a season, just the one, n' left the whole of em behind.{newline}Now most such tales are half made up n' liar's work the rest,{newline}but every one of em hath got a seed o' truth at best.{newline}Watch close, lad. I'll show thee what the old ones had in mind,{newline}n' thou shalt never doubt again what tellin's left behind.

Now this one I am proud of, because it technically shouldn't work! Ordinarily, quicksilver refuses to be a solid, which every child discovers by spilling it and drinking it, and yet if you hold Chamon just right it will hold an edge for exactly as long as your concentration does. Armor becomes irrelevant. Do you know how sharp a blade one atom thick is? Plate, mail, scale, bones, all sliced through so beautifully. I have never been able to keep one longer than a minute but trust me you won't need it.

Pick your ground. Not the men, the ground. Bring the light straight down onto that spot and hold it there, and everything standing beneath will be incinerated with great prejudice. Mind your placement, be exact. Light falls where you put it, not where you meant to put it.

No hands for this one, only your eyes and your patience. Fix your gaze upon a man and do not look away. The light pours out of you for as long as you lock your gaze. Blink and it ends. Most Wizlets blink.

The most popular spell on the battlefield and the least understood. Your body already heals itself constantly and slowly at the pace your flesh can afford. But Ghyran has no concept of affordability. Force the whole month of mending into a moment and the wound will vanish before your eyes. Worry about the aftereffects later, once the battle is won.

Shyish and a little Aqshy, I'm sure you've seen the Pyromancers use something like this. Except their mixture is wrong, you need a lot more death and a lot less fire, but they're too proud to admit it. It's almost frustrating to see how close they come and yet refuse to take the final step. Get the ratio right and the skull comes out as acid. A formation that hears this thing coming will break before it even arrives, and anyone caught in its path will wish they burned to death instead.

This one you hold in your hand before you use it, which is precisely as unwise as it sounds. Build the flame in your palm, let it grow until it hurts, then release it across everything standing in front of you. Do not hesitate. Hesitation is how a Pyromancer learns what his own hand smells like.

Blood mixed with Dhar makes for a wonderful combination. Open a vein and do not be squeamish about it, let it all squirt out! It will come out dark and deadly, cling to your foes, and burn them! You will feel weaker afterward, oh you poor little morsel. But then you will feel wonderful. And you'll want to do it again!

Keep your eyes forward. The light does not care for your feelings about your adversary, it only asks whether he should be there. Point it at the corrupt and it will purify them from this world. You will find it burns hottest on the undead and demonic. They are the only things that ever truly refuse us. I take it personally.

Every magister sneers at Minor Magic, including me at one point. But consider what a village hedge caster actually does. They have no order and no discipline so they grab a little of everything all at once. Some may call it Dhar, but with a bit of training and some manners it is Qhaysh. Ward of Arrows is the crude form of what I am about to teach you. This polished shield does not shelter one man, it shelters an entire army. Many a wizard has died to a stray projectile, and this will save you and your men from an undignified end to your careers.

I watched a boar die in a bramble once. Nothing killed it and it thrashed and thrashed. The thorns took a little each time it tried harder to free itself. Give your soldiers that bramble and every enemy who strikes them becomes the boar. They will swing, and they will bleed, and they will swing again, and they will bleed.

The simplest thing this order can do, and still there's nothing quite like it in this world. Balance the eight until they surrender their colors and throw the result. You can't rightly call it fire, or lightning, or rot. It is the colorless raw energy which underpins all other magic and whatever it touches is snuffed the way you would pinch out a candle. You may pour more in if you like and the sphere grows accordingly. There is no upper limit that I have found, only a limit to what I have been willing to attempt indoors.

Azyr, Shyish, and a measure of necromantic energy. Three ingredients and the third is usually what gets people executed. But I can assure you no one will live to tell the tale. Hold them together and let the mixture fall rather than fly. What comes down can be best described as soul lightning and it burns all material living or otherwise. Slower than a bolt but it covers more ground and lasts far longer. Use it at chokepoints for great effect.

This one kills slowly but perhaps "kill" is not the right word. Gather Ghyran and Shyish, life and death, into a man's body and leave it there, and his soul will slowly unzip from his flesh. It will only take a few seconds, and he'll keep fighting for most of the process, but eventually his being will split in two leaving his soul ripe for the taking. Do with it what you wish.

No blade in this one, lad, no bolt, no burnin' brand ta cast.{newline}Just thy will against another's till the weaker of em's passed.{newline}The stronger of the two drinks deep, the lesser one runs dry.{newline}I've seen a farmhand's stubbornness undo a knight thereby.{newline}So choose thy man with care, for armor hath no word ta say.{newline}It's thou what's bein' weighed in this. Pick wrong n' thou shalt pay.

Wait for them to break, and in the moment the line sags and men start to panic, then bring the rain. All of them at once will be mended where they stand. Your enemy will despair and that is when you will crush them. Into paste. Food for the fungi.
So you wish to fight like a mindless beast? An Amber Wizard in the making I see.

You have felt this before. A field in high summer. No wind and the air thick enough to lean on. The desire to lie down and nap. Bless your enemies with the sensation and they will slow to a stumble and cook inside the metal they are so proud of. A gentle spark would set them completely alight. Summer kills as many as winter, yet no one seems to notice or care.

Look at the ground, morsel. Look at it! Everywhere you have ever walked someone or something died, what do you think fertilizes all these beautiful little flowers? Push Dhar into the soil and up they come! Oh the sound of it, that first wet crack as the earth gives them back! Here's the best part: they do not ask why. They never ask why. Give me a plague pit and a bad afternoon and I will hand you an army, and every single one of them will tear a living man apart the moment you point.

Nothing in a thicket wants you to pass through it. No that's not poetry, it's just what a thicket is. Call it up under a man's feet and it will have his ankles before he understands what happened. He will hack at it. It grows faster than he swings. There is no fancy incantation for this one. It's just a thicket.

There was a taster in a lord's employ, a cautious sort o' man.{newline}Sipped from every cup n' bowl afore his master's meal began.{newline}But Shyish don't come in a cup, nor in the meat nor bread.{newline}It comes up through the marrow, lad. It's always been thy bed.

No doubt you will hear that the great vortex is the origin of all magic but this is a common misconception. The vortex only divides the raw magic which leaks out of that wound and into our world. I cannot help you find it and you would gain nothing by standing in front of it. But the principle scales down, and a Loremaster who understands the concept can conjure a miniature vortex of their own. What forms will divide and pull everything apart, caring not for allegiances. Do mind your footing.

Everyone's got a beast inside them. I'm not speaking metaphorically. It's just an older part of us that existed long before we learned to speak. Let it out. Your men will stop thinking and start doing, faster and stronger and entirely unbothered by the pain. Only they won't remember much afterward, which could be for the best.

Close your eyes. What do you feel? Beneath the wind on your face. Everything around you is straining upward. The moss, the roots, the mould in your boots, all of it pushing because it knows nothing else. That pressure is Ghyran and it is already inside you. Open your eyes and let it out, and whatever you look at will be bored clean through.

The common bolt takes what the storm offers. This one does not ask. Gather Azyr in your fist until it protests, then loose it in a single stroke that leaves nothing standing in the space it occupied... a whole rank, unmade between heartbeats. Do mind your footing lest you be devoured.

The dead are slow and patient, morsel, what a waste. This is how you whip them into shape! Lash the Dhar through your servants and they will surge forward out of turn, faster than a living man expects, striking again and again, wearing the enemy down. The living are fragile things, you see. But be warned, pushing your servants will make them come apart faster. Let them! Then raise some more! There are always more.
A paltry charm that can be surprisingly effective on the battlefield. This one is a bit of a prank.

Azyr is a wind before it is anything else, and a wind may simply be pushed. There is no artistry here, just a great and sudden shove. Loose it into a line of charging knights and watch them topple from their horses. Even an oracle must be permitted his vulgar indulgences.

Now stand back and let me show you my favorite. It begins as a single point and then it spreads and spreads, like a plague of locusts across the battlefield, devouring all the living and even some of the dead. No wounds or blood, just men folding over in rows, bodies falling by the score, fresh corpses for the grinder! Mind your own troops. Or don't! I have never been precious about the difference. You do find me precious, yes?
The Lady's ward pulls you back from death.

15% extra magic damage and magic resistance, 30% to grant nearby troops the same boons for a short time upon dealing damage
50% extra damage when striking at the backs of enemies. Same bonus applies to unaware enemies hit from any angle
Requires War Sails. Crew of a sinking or burning ship flee to the nearest safe ship by running across a bridge or swimming, preferring their own but boarding an enemy vessel if they must.
Swaps Amber Spear for a magic javelin that scales off Throwing and Spellcraft.
Lets casters channel to recharge Winds of Magic, at the cost of being sluggish and vulnerable while they do. Higher caster levels reduce the drawbacks. Affects enemy and companion wizards too.
Changes how much armor weight slows Winds of Magic recharge.
-100% removes the armor penalty. 0% keeps default. 200% triples the armor penalty.

Recharges Winds of Magic for yourself, allies, and enemies while you are in a battle or town scene. Recharge rate depends on derived stats. Only works if you have a real time mod like Time Pass enabled.
Fire damage per second to anyone on an ablaze deck. Default 4.
Requires War Sails. When a ship is set ablaze, anyone standing on its deck takes fire damage over time until they get off. Vanilla leaves the crew unharmed on a burning ship.
Slows the battle to 30 percent speed while you aim or charge a spell. Turn it off to keep the game at full speed while you cast.

Lets your clan companions and family use magic and appear in the spellbook's hero cycle. Turning it off later keeps their learned lores, spells and Winds intact for when you turn it back on. The main hero is always a caster.
Lag and crash protection. Lower it if huge spells stutter or freeze. Higher resolves big spells faster, but is the riskiest setting here.
Enchant items with the magical lores you know. Town enchanter's quarters, blueprint books, reagent drops, and enchanted gear on rival wizards.
Bodies that can burst at once
How many bodies come apart at once. Capped by Spell deaths resolved at once, under Performance.
Scales how often a spell kill bursts a body apart. 100% is the default rate, 0% turns it off.
Big spell kills can blow a body apart or scatter a skeleton into bones. Bombardments pack the most punch while hexes never dismember. Heroes are never affected.
Scales how often a spell kill scatters skeletons into bones. 130% is the default rate, 0% turns it off.
When to show the bottom left spell and Winds of Magic panel in battle.
Victorious battles can reward a fallen enemy's weapon or armor bearing a random enchantment.
Surviving units you mind controlled during a battle join your party afterward. Heroes never join. The in battle Mind Control spell works regardless of this setting.
How many enchanting reagents defeated enemies drop, as a percent of the default rate.
Fills the world with wizard lords who cast in battle. Each clan's tradition is fixed for the campaign. Off stops them casting.
How common wizard lords are. Picking a preset fills in the Advanced sliders. Editing a slider switches this to Custom.
Chance each lord of a great house is secretly a master of Dark or High Magic. At least one of each always exists. Editing this switches Magic Density to Custom.
Predicts what your current settings and seed would produce, by tradition. Reads the screen, so you can try numbers first. It does not describe the wizards your save already has.
Percent of eligible lords who are wizards. Editing this switches Magic Density to Custom.
By Clan gives every wizard clan its own lore. By Culture gives a whole faction the same lore, so Vlandia or Battania read as a single order. Applies on the next load.
Houses below this clan tier never field wizards. 0 means any house can. Applies to every density setting.
Lets mercenary companies and outlaw bands field wizards too. Off keeps magic to the great houses.
Shifts how strong the world's wizards are. Zero is the default setting with no change. Your own clan is never affected, and hidden masters stay at full strength.
Caps how many skeletons an AI necromancer can raise from one battle, as a percent of his party size limit.
Puts the Rival Wizards settings back to their defaults. Press Done to apply them.
Allows faction leaders to be wizards. Turn off for a world where only lesser nobles practise magic. Applies on the next load.
The seed your world is built from. Determines who becomes a wizard. Clear it for your own seed.
Percent of wandering companions who start as wizards. Editing this switches Magic Density to Custom.
Requires the War Sails expansion. When on, your spells damage enemy ship hulls, set them ablaze, and shred their sails in naval battles. When off, magic only harms the crew.
Scales how much damage your spells deal to ships. 100% is the tuned default and 0% is the same as turning ship damage off.
The enchanter's quarter stocks blueprint books, rotating weekly by the town's ruling lore and prosperity. Turn off to learn only from drops and masters.
The enchanter's quarter stocks a small weekly supply of enchanting reagents. Turn off to make reagents drop only.
Enables the resurrection of fallen enemies as skeletons after victorious battles.
Spell damage skips bystanders such as arena spectators, townsfolk and merchants. Anyone actively fighting you is still a valid target.
Shows a battle log line for your spell damage, healing, and friendly fire, colored by element.
Adds a flat bonus to your Spell Effectiveness (scales spell damage and healing).
Percent added to Spell Effectiveness. -100% means spells deal no damage, 0% is unchanged, 200% adds triple.
The spellbook screen no longer sells anything beyond Minor Magic. Seek out wizard lords and learn from them instead. Does nothing while Rival Wizards is off.
Which attribute governs the Spellcraft skill's learning rate. Takes effect after a restart. Default Intelligence.
What fighting a battle alongside an order's wizard earns you, counted only once per battle.
What executing one of an order's wizards costs you with it. Killing one in battle does not count.
What releasing one of an order's captured wizards earns you. Ransoms and escapes do not count.
How much of a standing change also influences each lord's relation in that order.
How much learning a whole lore moves your standing. Orders that favour that lore approve, rivals take offense.
How much learning a single spell moves your standing. Orders that favour that lore approve, rivals take offense.
How much Winds of Magic each spell kill grants.
Gives Winds of Magic on a spell kill. Player only.
